$note: A copy taken at seq S and fed rows S..N equals the gateway at the watermark — every replicated table, VALUES not bytes (#1020, D-1020-D1-11). Hand-authored rather than generated: the claim is a comparison between two FILES, which is not a row dump. `crates/vault/tests/gates.rs` runs it; `crates/seat` (lane D2) runs the same file against the seat-side applier, which is the same function.
$whyValuesNotBytes: Two SQLite files holding the same rows are not byte-identical: page order, free pages and the WAL all differ, and a VACUUM changes the bytes without changing an answer. The claim that matters is that every replicated table answers the same, so the comparison is per-table, per-row, per-column.

script.$note: Phase one runs before the copy is taken; phase two runs after, and is what the copy has to catch up on. Every timestamp is explicit so the run is deterministic — the touch trigger writes the wall clock when a statement leaves `updated_at` alone.
